title: Counting heavy pairs in a 3-uniform hypergraph
statement:
Let $H$ be a $3$-uniform hypergraph on the vertex set $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$, so that every edge of $H$ has exactly three vertices, and let $d$ be a positive integer. Call a two-element set $Q = \{u,v\}$ of vertices *heavy* if its degree exceeds $d$, that is, if more than $d$ edges of $H$ contain $Q$, and let $P$ denote the collection of all heavy pairs. Then
\[
  \abs{P} \cdot d \;\le\; 3\,\abs{H}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: H is 3-uniform (every edge has exactly 3 vertices)
heavy pairs P are the 2-element vertex sets Q with degree_H(Q) > d
replaced:
Let $H$ be a $3$-uniform hypergraph on $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ and let $d > 0$. Then the number
of heavy pairs satisfies
\[
  \abs{P} \cdot d \;\le\; 3 \, \abs{H},
\]
where $P$ is the set of pairs of degree more than $d$; equivalently $\abs{P} \le 3m/d$
for $m = \abs{H}$ edges, since each $3$-edge contributes exactly three pairs.
